notes.summary: Intrinsic compact primary boundary, support-safe finite lifting, exact conductor fibres and completion; nilpotents are invisible and dimension zero is empty.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the primary-gauge cocycle, finite lifting including nonminimal supports, the finite/infinite conductor identification, and the all-semivaluation completion homeomorphism with exact completed-primary contraction. No positivity descent is inferred merely from topological descent.
notes.text:
For a Noetherian local ring (R,m), use real semivaluations v:R→[0,∞] satisfying the usual multiplicative and ultrametric axioms and 0<v(m)<∞. Their support is any prime strictly below m, without a minimal-prime restriction. Ideal values are minima over finite generators; changing generators proves independence, v(IJ)=v(I)+v(J), and v(I+J)=min(v(I),v(J)). Units have value zero. Proper primary means primary for the marked maximal ideal.

Fix a proper primary ideal a. The section V_a={v:v(a)=1} is compact Hausdorff. For a=m this follows from the closed semivaluation conditions in the compact product [0,∞]^R. If m^r⊂a⊂m^s, then s v(m)≤v(a)≤r v(m), so rescaling gives a homeomorphism between sections. Every primary gauge is finite positive continuous and bounded. For another primary b, H_ab(v)=v/v(b), and a homogeneous function transforms by u_b(H_ab(v))=u_a(v)/v(b). The denominator and its inverse are bounded; substitution proves the exact three-gauge cocycle. The centred cone is the product of its section and its positive radial coordinate, so the section represents the intrinsic ray quotient. Nonprimary ideals give only their open finite-value domains, potentially noncompact; unit and zero ideals have no level-one section.

Nilpotents have infinite value; comparison of f+n with f proves invariance under reduction. A zero-dimensional local reduction is a field with empty boundary. In positive dimension, a penultimate prime in a saturated chain gives a one-dimensional excellent domain quotient. Its finite normalization has a local DVR whose order supplies a boundary point. Ordinary background used here and subsequently includes lying over, prime avoidance, finite Artinian decomposition, and excellence's localization/quotient stability, Nagata finiteness and universal catenarity. No arbitrary-characteristic resolution follows.

A nonzero reduced finite injection R⊂B gives continuous surjective restriction V_aB(B)→V_a(R), using the finite union of closed-centre sections upstairs. Given v with support p, choose P above p, pass FIRST to the finite field extension Frac(B/P)/Frac(R/p), and extend its valuation ring. Take the integral closure, a prime above the valuation maximal ideal, and a dominating valuation ring. The domination assertion has the usual Zorn proof: in a maximal dominating local subring C, if adjoining x^{-1} makes its maximal ideal the unit ideal, an equation 1=Σ a_i x^{-i}, with a_i in that ideal, makes x integral after multiplying by a power and dividing by 1-a_0. Lying over then permits adjoining x and localizing, contradicting maximality unless one of x,x^{-1} was already present. The extended ring intersects the old field in the original valuation ring. An algebraic equation for a new nonzero element has two least-valued terms, so an integer multiple of its value is in the old real value group. Division by that integer, checked using common multiples, embeds the extended group order-preservingly in R. A monic equation shows integral elements have nonnegative value. Compose with B→B/P and assign P infinite value. This retains nonminimal supports rather than extending an unsupported semivaluation to the original fraction field. Compactness makes restriction a quotient map.

For finite normalization S, the conductor c=(R:S) contains a regular element, obtained by clearing denominators of finite generators. It is an ideal of both rings and R=S×_{S/c}(R/c): an element of S whose residue comes from R differs from an R-element by an element of c. Normalization branches are local normal CENTRES above m. Chinese-remainder elements separating these centres give open positive-value loci; the finitely many pieces are clopen. They are not indexed merely by minimal primes.

If v(c)<∞, choose c∈c of finite value. Every lift has w(s)=v(cs)-v(c), proving uniqueness with finite subtraction. If v(c)=∞, every lift kills c, and equality after restriction S/c→R/c is precisely the identification. The infinity stratum is CLOSED and its finite complement OPEN, without a closedness claim for the complement. Fibre-constant continuous functions descend continuously by the compact quotient; extended nonpositive upper semicontinuous functions descend upper semicontinuously because closed superlevel sets have compact images. This supplies no positivity descent by itself.

Completion preserves the entire boundary. For F∈Rhat choose representatives F_N modulo m^N and put d=v(m)>0. Differences have value ≥Nd. If some value is below Nd, later values stabilize; otherwise they tend to infinity. Define vhat(F) by this limit. Then min(vhat(F),Nd)=min(v(F_N),Nd), proving uniqueness, independence and the sum/product axioms. For q(t)=t/(1+t), q(∞)=1, these continuous truncations approximate q(vhat(F)) uniformly within (1+N/r)^{-1}. Thus completion restriction is a homeomorphism. Every completed primary J contains mhat^N; representatives of its generators modulo that power belong to J∩R and, together with m^N, generate J. Hence J=(J∩R)Rhat. The quotient isomorphism also proves exact contraction of extended primary ideals. Unit-or-primary profiles and their uniform/decreasing classes agree under completion; no equivalence of model categories is asserted.

Swanson–Huneke 6.4.1–2 were checked completely and agree with the domination argument. Artifacts: n1.md, argument.md and P12.2-paper.tex/PDF. Rerun: python audit_inputs.py; python build_delivery.py. These are draft mathematical arguments; execution is not verification.

notes.summary: Exact integral-dependence, Rees/dimension and analytically irreducible-domain applications, including zero-dimensional and unit qualifications.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses the current July 2024 Swanson–Huneke author PDF and exact Rond–Spivakovsky v1 at their stated hypotheses. Proves a common exponent by finite graded generation. Zero-dimensional boundaryless components require a zero-image condition; units avoid the literal strict remark.
notes.text:
Use n1. Published applications below are at exact hypotheses, with complete immediate units checked; recursive historical proofs are disclosed rather than claimed independently reconstructed.

The current July 2024 Swanson–Huneke author PDF, complete 6.8.1–4, gives this consequence: for Noetherian semilocal E, an ideal J containing a boundary power, and finite ideal Q, if w(Q)≥w(J) on every normalized centred semivaluation and Q has zero image on each zero-dimensional minimal component where J is nonunit, then Q⊂integral-closure(J). Apply the centred-DVR criterion on each positive-dimensional local domain component and the all-minimal-components criterion. The zero-dimensional qualification is essential because those components have no boundary. In every conductor application Q=K(aE)^L with L>0, ensuring the required zero image. Unit components impose no condition. For nonreduced E, lift the componentwise monic equations, multiply over finitely many minimal primes, and raise to a power to kill the nilpotent error. Coefficients retain the required ideal powers. Complete 1.1.5 was checked. Visual inspection of printed page 140 restored extraction-omitted integral-closure bars.

A common exponent is proved directly. Each qt for q∈Q is integral over E[Jt] by its homogeneous equation, so E[(J+Q)t] is a finite graded E[Jt]-module. Choose homogeneous generators of degrees ≤h. Its degree N+h coefficients lie in J^{N+h-d}⊂J^N. Thus Q^{N+h}⊂(J+Q)^{N+h}⊂J^N for every N≥1. This works with nilpotents and does not assume finite normalized Rees algebra. Complete 1.2.3–5 was also checked, with printed page 6 inspected for closure bars.

Complete 10.2.2, including the proof ending at 10.2.3, constructs centred Rees DVRs for nonzero proper primary ideals of positive-dimensional excellent local domains. Complete 10.4.3 gives residue transcendence degree dim A−1 under formal equidimensionality. Excellence gives universal catenarity; complete B.5.1 and proof identify its needed domain consequence with local formal equidimensionality. B.3.2 and its immediate context give, for finite-type birational B over excellent local domain A and P∩A=m, dim B_P+trdeg_{A/m}κ(P)=dim A. The book describes the proof as a modification of an earlier argument. Historical Mori–Nagata, Ratliff and Rees dependencies are disclosed.

The complete immediate Stacks 0C23 lemma/proof gives normal completion for normal Noetherian local rings with normal formal fibres. Excellence suffices, so an excellent normal local domain has domain completion and is analytically irreducible and unramified. Its referenced Algebra 10.163.8 was not recursively read. This is not asserted for arbitrary nonnormal domains.

Exact Rond–Spivakovsky 1404.4885v1, complete pages 1–2, Definitions 1.1–1.2 and Theorems 1.3, 1.4, 1.7, applies to this analytically irreducible DOMAIN. For a centred divisorial ν and maximal-ideal Rees valuations ν_j, Izumi–Rees gives ν(f)≤c_jν_j(f). Set C_0=max_j c_jν_j(m). The asymptotic-order formula and order-error theorem yield ν(f)≤C_0 min_j[ν_j(f)/ν_j(m)]=C_0 orderbar_m(f)≤C_0(order_m(f)+K). For nonzero nonunits, order≥1 and is finite by Krull intersection, giving ν(f)≤C_0(1+K)order_m(f). Units have both values zero and are separate; literal strict Remark 1.6 is not used. Swanson's entire Rees-valuations Section 5 was checked: 5.2 is complete-domain only. The general analytic-domain application uses exact Rond–Spivakovsky 1.3. Original Rees 1989 and historical Izumi proofs were not independently read.

notes.summary: Separate P/Q/C/D conventions, uniform lattice density and a support-safe coefficient norm trace with proved full fibre support.
notes.detailedSummary: Generic inseparable lengths and quotient-support Gauss coefficient minima give choice-independent positive traces and exact normal-target C/D descent. No defectless e*f formula, arbitrary increasing closure, or raw descent is assumed.
notes.text:
Use n1. Let P_R be finite nonnegative REAL combinations of gauges of ideals containing a boundary power, with the unit allowed; Q_R=−P_R. Let C_R be its uniform closure among finite continuous functions. Let D_R consist of infima of nonempty decreasing C_R-nets, including zero and the identically bottom function. Finite semilocal algebras use product classes over their closed centres. Local primary ideals contract to ideals primary at their own centre and unit at others; tuples glue in a common Artinian boundary quotient. Denominators synchronize by powers. Rational profiles −v(I)/k are uniformly dense in C_R by rational approximation of finite real coefficients and product ideals. C is a closed convex cone stable under maxima by ideal sums. D is upper semicontinuous and stable under addition, positive scaling and finite maxima using product directed sets. No increasing-limit closure, arbitrary-infimum closure or nested-net flattening is assumed.

The rational difference span is a lattice: after a common denominator its expressions are (v(I)−v(J))/k, and min(v(I)−v(J),v(K)−v(H))=v(IH+KJ)−v(JH). It contains rational constants and separates points using v((f)+a^N)=min(v(f),N), with centre-separating ideals semilocally. Its UNIFORM closure is a real vector lattice. The compact lattice proof gives all continuous real functions: affine combinations of a separating function match a continuous target at two points; rational approximations preserve strict local error tests. For each first point use finitely many minima to control the target everywhere while matching nearby, then finitely many maxima over first-point neighbourhoods. Negation interchanges the bounds. This does not assert an integer ideal formula for arbitrary irrational finite spans.

Let A be excellent normal local domain, A⊂B finite domain extension, K⊂L its fraction fields, n=[L:K]. For a B-ideal J choose finite A-module generators b_i and define N(J) as the coefficient ideal of the polynomial norm N_{L(T)/K(T)}(ΣT_i b_i). In a finite field M containing all embedding images, this polynomial is ∏_σ(ΣT_iσ(b_i))^q, with generic inseparable length q and q|Σ|=n. The formula follows by decomposing L⊗K Kbar into Artinian factors: determinant of multiplication on a length-q factor is its residue scalar to power q. Coefficients are integral over A and lie in K, hence in A by normality. Linear substitutions in both directions prove independence of generators. If J contains a^N B, add base generators x redundantly: the pure-variable coefficient is x^n, so N(J) contains a boundary power.

Let E normalize A in M. Lift ANY base semivaluation to E by n1, including nonzero support, and compose with embeddings to obtain w_σ on B. Minimum coefficient values multiply: quotient by support, enter its valued quotient fraction field, divide each nonzero polynomial by a coefficient of least finite value, and reduce to nonzero residue polynomials. Their product is nonzero. A polynomial zero modulo support has infinite coefficient minimum and causes no difficulty. Therefore v(N(J))=qΣ_σ w_σ(J) on EVERY support. Boundary-power ideals keep these sums finite.

Define μ_v=qΣ_σ δ_{w_σ}, mass n. Its gauge integrals are fixed by the coefficient identity. Uniform density and equal mass make it independent of the lift on every continuous function, hence as a finite measure. Its support is the FULL restriction fibre: any fibre point on B extends to E by n1, with the identity embedding of B, and occurs with positive weight. Choice independence puts it in every such measure's support. Thus the entire fibre is finite, cardinality ≤n. This uses generic inseparable lengths, not assumed valuationwise defectless ramification/residue-degree identities.

TH(v)=∫H dμ_v is positive, continuous-valued and norm n. Continuity holds on gauges by the coefficient formula, then on all continuous functions by density and the mass bound. It preserves C, taking −w(J)/k to −v(N(J))/k. Finite positive sums commute with decreasing nonpositive extended limits: a bottom summand forces bottom, and otherwise directedness approximates all finite limits simultaneously. Thus fibre-constant C_B or D_B functions descend using T/n to the same respective base class, with an ACTUAL decreasing net for D.

For an arbitrary reduced source finite over normal local A, choose dominating minimal components, normalize them and sum their traces divided by total generic degree. At every base point the traced values equal the descended function by constancy on the FULL original fibre. Vertical components receive no fabricated generic degree, but remain constrained by that full constancy. This proves exact normal-target C/D descent. Ideal extension and limits give the converse. Every lift has the same base primary denominator, so the result respects n1's gauge cocycle.

notes.summary: Uniform C descent for every excellent reduced finite injection, with full conductor quotient coverage and compact open covers.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses positive boundary factors, all minimal components, a common integral-dependence exponent and exact residue contraction. Finite-conductor estimates are never applied at infinity. Internally increasing negative profiles establish uniform approximation, not increasing-limit completion.
notes.text:
Use n1–n3. For every excellent reduced local R and nonzero reduced finite injection R⊂B, pullback is an isometry and f*C_R={u∈C_B constant on every restriction fibre}.

Induct on target dimension. Dimension zero has empty sections; normal targets are n3. First prove normalization descent using the finite-injection theorem in lower dimensions, then arbitrary injections by normalization base change. Let S normalize R, c be its conductor, C_0=R/c and E=S/c. A regular conductor element gives dim C_0<dim R. C_0⊂E remains injective after reduction because nilpotence is detected in the injected subring. Restriction of primary profiles and uniform limits to quotient sections preserves classes. A fibre-compatible u∈C_S descends continuously to h by n1, and induction gives h_0∈C_{C_0}. If the quotient boundary is empty, conductor values are finite everywhere and quotient estimates are omitted.

Fix ε>0. Choose synchronized rational profiles j=−w(J)/k and κ=−v(K)/k approximating u and h_0 within ε. Make J proper at each positive-dimensional centre by an arbitrarily small negative boundary correction, starting with smaller errors. Enlarge the common denominator until 1/k<ε. On every quotient boundary point |w(K_E)−w(J_E)|<2kε. Choose integer L with 2kε<L≤2kε+1. Q=K_E(aE)^L then has w(Q)≥w(J_E). The POSITIVE boundary factor gives zero image on zero-dimensional nonunit minimal components. N2 therefore gives Q integral over J_E, including nonreduced E, and one h' with Q^{N+h'}⊂J_E^N for all N.

Set I_N=J^N∩R, a proper primary ideal. The conductor fibre product proves EXACTLY (I_N+c)/c=J_E^N∩C_0. For the nontrivial inclusion lift a residue to an element of J^N; because that residue comes from C_0, the same element belongs to R. The image contains K^{N+h'}(aC_0)^{L(N+h')}.

At conductor-INFINITE points quotient values consequently give v(I_N)/(kN)≤(1+h'/N)(v(K)/k+L/k), all finite terms. At conductor-FINITE points the unique lift w and cJ^N⊂I_N give w(J)/k≤v(I_N)/(kN)≤w(J)/k+v(c)/(kN). The last estimate is used ONLY when v(c) is finite. Everywhere, I_N⊂J^N gives v(I_N)/(kN)≥−h−ε. The limit upper bound is ≤−h+4ε: use the quotient approximation and L/k<3ε at infinity, and j at finite conductor.

The continuous b_n=v(I_{2^n})/(k2^n) decrease because I_N²⊂I_{2N}. Their increasing strict-test open sets {b_n+h<5ε} cover the compact section. One n covers it all, and the common lower bound gives ||−b_n−h||<5ε. Thus h∈C_R. The negative profiles INCREASE internally; no increasing-limit closure or decreasing regularization is asserted here.

For arbitrary R⊂B form B'=(B⊗R S)_red. Base change of the integral surjective spectrum map is surjective, so its kernel in reduced S is zero. Pullback of u is fibre constant over each normal local centre of S; n3 descends it to C_S, precisely the pullback of h. Normalization descent gives h∈C_R, closing induction. Ideal extension supplies the converse, and surjectivity gives the isometry.

Let N_R denote continuous functions whose normalization pullbacks are compatible RAW local negative real ideal profiles. Only Q_R⊂N_R⊂C_R and closure(Q_R)=closure(N_R)=C_R are concluded; raw equality is not. All conductor-infinite and nonminimal supports remain.

notes.summary: Unbounded everywhere-negative D descent by finite-gap insertion and an actual decreasing continuous-majorant net.
notes.detailedSummary: Covers partialbottom and discontinuous unbounded limits. Uses finite positive gaps even for allbottom. Internal increasing contractions select a single approximant; insertion constructs the actual decreasing completion without flattening.
notes.text:
Use n1–n4. A fibre-constant u∈D_B descends to D_R when its descent h is everywhere strictly negative, including partialbottom and unbounded discontinuous functions. Compact upper semicontinuity gives h≤−c for some FINITE c>0. Allbottom is directly the limit of −N v(a); zero is separate. Normal targets follow n3. Induct on dimension as in n4, first normalization then arbitrary injections by reduced normalization base change. Quotient restrictions descend by lower-dimensional induction to h_0∈D_{C_0}.

Prove insertion: for each finite continuous F>h, find q∈C_R with h<q<F. Choose a FINITE positive lower bound e for the lower semicontinuous gap F−h, for example below half the minimum of 1 and its infimum. If that infimum is infinite, e stays finite; no infinity subtraction occurs.

From the decreasing continuous representation of u, compact strict-test covers and directedness select g with u≤g<−c/2 and g<F∘ρ−e/2. Choose 0<b<1/2 with b||g||<e/8. Scaling (1−b)g remains below F−e/4 and exceeds finite u by ≥bc/2. A sufficiently close rational approximation j=−w(J)/k remains strictly negative and gives a fixed s>0 with u+s≤j<F∘ρ−e/8. The first inequality is automatic at bottom. J is proper at every centre; put M=||j||.

For arbitrarily small δ>0 construct a quotient rational profile κ≥h_0 with κ∘ρ_E<j_E+δ. Choose b_1 with b_1M<s/4 and a decreasing C_{C_0}-net g_i→h_0. Since u_E≤j_E−s, its scaled limit (1−b_1)u_E<j_E−s/4. Compactness selects one scaled term below j_E−s/8 throughout E and simultaneously g_i<−c/2 on C_0. Scaling raises it uniformly above finite h_0; rational approximation within min(b_1c/4,s/16) gives κ, even with a negative gap below j_E. Synchronize denominators and enlarge k until 1/k<δ. Empty quotient boundary requires no construction.

Take integer L with kδ<L≤kδ+1. Q=K_E(aE)^L has values dominating J_E. N2 gives integral dependence, including zero-dimensional components, and a common exponent h'. Contract I_N=J^N∩R. N4's exact residue identity gives liminf[−v(I_N)/(kN)]≥κ−2δ≥h−2δ at conductor infinity. At finite conductor its finite estimate gives limit j≥h+s. The dyadic f_n=−v(I_{2^n})/(k2^n) increase, are finite continuous and satisfy f_n≤j. The open sets {f_n>h−3δ} cover the compact section, including bottom points, since h is upper semicontinuous. Choose one n valid everywhere.

Choose δ so η=3δ/c<1/2 and ηM<e/16, and set q=(1−η)f_n∈C_R. At finite h≤−c, q>(1−η)(h−3δ)≥h+ηc−3δ(1−η)=h+3δη>h. At bottom q is finite. Also q≤(1−η)j≤j+ηM<F. This proves insertion by allowed positive scaling, not addition of a positive constant.

Let Qcal be all C_R-functions strictly above h. Zero belongs. For two members insert below their continuous minimum, which need not be psh, so Qcal is downward directed. At a point v and finite t>h(v), upper semicontinuity and compact Hausdorff normality give a finite continuous test F>h with F(v)<t: choose h(v)<ℓ<t and a neighbourhood with h<ℓ, then use a Urysohn cutoff to interpolate ℓ to a global strict upper bound outside. Insertion gives q(v)<t. Hence inf Qcal=h, and reverse pointwise order is an ACTUAL decreasing C_R-net to h. This closes normalization and finite-injection induction. No increasing completion or net flattening is invoked.

notes.summary: Divisorial density and the normal zero dichotomy yield full D descent, including mixedzero and every bottom pattern.
notes.detailedSummary: Support-safe ratio charts and the exact dimension/residue formula prove density. The active clopen indicator descends with positivity through bounded descent. Insertion produces an actual decreasing net rather than taking an increasing limit.
notes.text:
Use n1–n5. For every reduced nonzero finite injection over an excellent reduced local R, f*D_R={u∈D_B constant on every restriction fibre}, including allzero, allbottom, mixedzero, partialbottom, conductor-infinite and nonminimal supports.

First prove divisorial density on an excellent local domain A. A basic neighbourhood of v imposes finitely many strict coordinate tests. Choose a generator a_0 of a with v(a_0)=1 and include all a_j/a_0 in a finite-type birational algebra B_0⊂Frac(A). For each finite positive tested f choose rational bounds p/q<v(f)<r/s within the required interval and include f^q/a_0^p and a_0^r/f^s. For infinite coordinates include only the lower-bound ratio. Units and zero have fixed values. All denominators have finite value, so even a nonzero-support v extends nonnegatively to B_0. Its positive-value prime P contains a_0 and the strict-test ratios and contracts to m. The excellent domain (B_0)_P has positive dimension. N2 gives a centred Rees DVR ν; normalized by ν(a_0)=ν(a)>0, it satisfies every original strict test.

It is divisorial over A: the birational dimension formula gives dim(B_0)_P+trdeg_{A/m}κ(P)=dim A, while the Rees DVR has residue transcendence degree dim(B_0)_P−1 over κ(P). Transcendence degrees add to dim A−1. Its value group is discrete rank one and its A-centre is closed. This is the precise divisorial definition used in the order-bound source, proving density on the actual all-support section without singular SNC or resolution.

For normal A, n2 gives ν(f)≤C_ν order_m(f) on nonzero nonunits; units are zero separately. Normalize ν by a. If m^r⊂a, every v_0 has v_0(m)≥1/r. Choose a generator attaining a proper primary I's finite v_0-value. Then ν(I)≤C_ν r v_0(I). It also holds for units. Thus every finite real negative ideal combination and uniform limit g∈C_A satisfies g(ν)≥C_ν r g(v_0). If g(v_0)=0, nonpositivity forces zero at every divisorial point; density and continuity give g=0. If u=inf g_i has zero anywhere, every nonpositive g_i is zero there, hence everywhere. Each normal-centre completed function is therefore identically zero or everywhere negative, with bottom allowed; compactness supplies a finite negative upper bound for each active branch.

For normalization-fibre-compatible u∈D_S, call the everywhere-negative normal centres active. Active and inactive points cannot share a fibre. The tuple σ=−1 on active centres and zero elsewhere belongs to C_S by primary/unit gluing and is fibre compatible. N4 descends it WITH POSITIVITY to σ∈C_R. Thus T={σ=−1} is clopen, h=0 off T, and h≤−c on T for finite c>0. Empty T gives zero. If every active value is bottom, Nσ is already a decreasing sequence to h.

Otherwise u−δ is everywhere negative for each δ>0, so n5 gives h−δ∈D_R. Do NOT take their increasing limit. On compact T let finite continuous F>h have finite positive lower gap e. Choose 0<η<1/2 with η(||F||+e)<e/4 and δ=ηc/[2(1−η)]. At finite h≤−c, (1−η)(h−δ)=h+η(−h−c/2)>h; using h≤F−e also gives this scaled target <F−e/2, including bottom. A decreasing C_R-net g_i→h−δ has one term with (1−η)g_i<F−e/4 throughout T by compact strict-test covers. Choose N with −N<min_T F. Then q=max((1−η)g_i,Nσ)∈C_R is strictly between h and F on T and EXACTLY zero off T. At bottom q is finite; at finite points it dominates the strictly larger scaled target. Off T its second term is zero and its first nonpositive.

These majorants are downward directed by insertion below the continuous minimum, and the Urysohn construction on T makes their infimum h. Reverse pointwise order is an actual decreasing C_R-net. This proves full normalization descent without increasing closure or flattening.

For arbitrary R⊂B, pull back to (B⊗R S)_red, injective over S by n4. N3's normal-centre traces descend the fibre-compatible limit to D_S, exactly h pulled back from R. Full normalization descent gives h∈D_R. Ideal extension preserves uniform and decreasing limits and proves the converse. Gauge changes follow n1. Empty dimension-zero sections have their unique empty function.

notes.summary: G1–G3 discharged using exact Stacks units and corrected Keeler v5, with explicit real Cartier perturbation and rationalization.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite sections yield a fixed primary correction inside R. Corrected uniform generation applies to the full nonreduced fibre. Real nef perturbation, finite-span openness and a positive rational solution in a finitely generated Picard subgroup prove genuine Q-ampleness without global finite-rank assumptions.
notes.text:
Use n1. The three geometric inputs are proved using exact published immediate units, not supplied continuation labels.

Let Y be the actual blowup of a proper primary I on POSITIVE-DIMENSIONAL reduced Noetherian local R. Dimension zero is n1's empty case. No minimal component here is zero-dimensional, since that would make the maximal ideal minimal and force dimension zero. The Rees algebra is a subalgebra of R[t], hence reduced. Projection to component domains gives prime kernels with intersection zero; component-separating R-elements identify them as minimal primes. I is nonzero on each component, so each blowup component dominates one of R. The f-chart R[I/f]⊂R_f makes f regular and I=(f). Thus I O_Y=O(−E) for an ACTUAL effective Cartier E, with relatively ample tautological bundle. Y is projective and the identity away from m. Complete Stacks 29.38.4–5, 01VG, gives relative=absolute ampleness over affine base.

G1: complete Stacks 30.16.1 and 30.16.3, 0B5S, makes T=H0(Y,O_Y) a finite R-module. Reducedness and generic dominance embed it into the total quotient ring of R and include R injectively. H0 localizes: use a finite affine cover of separated Y, affine pairwise intersections, and the kernel of the difference map between finite products of affine section modules. Localization is exact and commutes with these finite products. Off m the blowup is the identity, so T/R is a finite module supported at m and killed by m^h. Fix ONCE c_0=m^{h+1}. Then c_0T⊂m⊂R AS ELEMENTS OF R: m^hT lies in R and one more m-factor lies in m. This correction is primary, not the full normalization conductor.

Its H coefficient is positive; omit zero terms. Rational-nef plus real-ample proves D+δH real-ample. For real δ use smaller positive rational δ_0 and add (δ−δ_0)H.

A+Σe_iL_i=(1−ΣN_i|e_i|)A+Σ|e_i|(N_iA+sign(e_i)L_i).
For a general real-ample sum reserve one positive summand sA and perturb that summand sufficiently little. This proves openness without a finite-rank claim about the whole Picard group.

notes.detailedSummary: Defines geometric positivity before comparison. Common primary models, actual order units and support-quotient lattices give evaluation. A fixed primary section correction proves continuity and uniform ideal approximation; no raw equality, arbitrary-model cofinality or radial identity is asserted.
notes.text:
Use n1, n3 and n7 for construction/comparison and n4–n6 for descent. Positive-dimensional local reduction is treated geometrically; dimension zero has the unique empty-boundary cone directly.

BEFORE comparison, define admissible models as ACTUAL primary blowups Y_I. On a model take D=−Σd_jA_j, d_j≥0, with A_j ACTUAL effective integral Cartier divisors supported on the closed fibre. Real Cartier means the integral Cartier group tensored with the REAL NUMBERS. Require deg_C D≥0 for EVERY contracted proper integral curve. This is actual Cartier effectivity and independent line-bundle degree positivity, not nonnormal Weil-coefficient effectivity or completed ideal membership.

The models are directed. On Y_IJ the product of pulled-back ideals is locally (f), f regular. Set J'=f^{-1}J in the total quotient sheaf; IJ'=O. Locally a finite sum of products equals one, so one ij' is a unit. For x∈I, xj'∈O and x=(xj')/(ij')·i; thus I is principal with regular generator, and J is its invertible inverse times (f). The blowup universal property gives maps to Y_I and Y_J. Actual effectivity pulls back. Curve degree pulls back to zero if the image is a point, or to the image degree times a positive field degree otherwise, preserving nefness.

E_I is an ACTUAL Cartier order unit. For exceptional integral F, the coherent quotients (O(F)+O)/O and (O(−F)+O)/O are supported on the closed fibre. On a finite cover a common power of I O kills both, giving O(F−NE)⊂O and O(−F−NE)⊂O. These invertible ideal subsheaves give actual effectivity, hence −NE≤F≤NE. Finite real spans inherit bounds.

For v with support p, pass to the valued field Frac(R/p). A least-finite-value generator f of I gives the centre on its blowup chart since a/f has nonnegative value. Overlap units or the universal property prove independence. Pull O(F) back to the spectrum of this field's valuation ring. At its generic point, outside the exceptional fibre, O(F) has its canonical trivialization as O. The pullback is therefore a rank-one lattice inside this quotient field. For its generator g define f_F(v)=−v(g). Different generators differ by valuation-ring units. This does NOT assume a homomorphism from the total quotient ring of R to Frac(R/p). Evaluation is additive, homogeneous, common-pullback invariant, finite by the order-unit bounds, and f_E=v(I). All nonminimal supports remain.

For negative rational relatively ample L, choose arbitrarily large divisible k with O(kL) generated. F_k=H0(O(kL)) lies in finite T because O(kL)⊂O and is a finite R-module. With n7's FIXED primary c_0 set J_k=c_0F_k⊂R. It is an R-ideal, proper because c_0T⊂m, and unit off m by localization and generation, hence proper primary. At every valued centre, global generation means one section coefficient is a unit. Consequently on ALL semivaluations
−v(J_k)/k=f_L−v(c_0)/k.
Every term is finite, and ||v(c_0)|| is bounded. This proves uniform primary-profile approximation of f_L.

For any integral exceptional F, G2 and actual order bounds choose N with L=F−NE both negative and ample. The section equality gives f_F=−v(J_k)/k+v(c_0)/k+Nv(I), proving continuity without assuming nonnormal coefficient continuity. Real evaluations are finite sums. Actual negative effectivity gives nonpositive evaluation.

Let M_geom be these independent negative curve-nef evaluations, including zero; C_geom is their uniform closure and D_geom their ACTUAL decreasing-net completion. For D=−Σd_jA_j, n7 makes D−δE real-ample for every δ>0. Round every nonnegative coefficient UP to nearby rationals, retaining ampleness by finite-span openness and actual negativity. The resulting rational D' is genuinely Q-ample by n7. Bounded continuous evaluations make f_D' uniformly close to f_D as δ and rounding errors shrink. The fixed-primary section formula, then divisible k→∞, proves M_geom⊂C_R; it never divides an infinite conductor value.

Conversely every finite REAL negative ideal combination is geometric: pull its exceptional divisors to a common product blowup. Each E_i is actually effective and −E_i is pulled back from an ample bundle, hence curve-nef. Unit terms are zero. Therefore Q_R⊂M_geom⊂C_R, C_geom=C_R and D_geom=D_R. This is the additional comparison theorem demanded by P12.2; core positivity was independently geometric before any completion. Raw equality is not asserted.

The admissible primary-model system is precise. No cofinality in arbitrary proper birational models, nonnormal Weil substitute, singular SNC or positive-characteristic resolution is claimed. Finite core pullback follows extended boundary ideals and the same degree rule; n1 and n4–n6, together with comparison, give full primary and conductor rules without raw descent. Envelopes, products, energy and CLD/classical radial identification are not supplied.

notes.summary: Full smooth BFJ recovery on ALL semivaluations at the exact smooth affine algebraically closed characteristic-zero hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses substantive closed-simplex continuity, corrected unit/eventual proper-primary approximation, minimal-face relative interiors and all-retraction infima. Bottom, smooth DVR and empty dimension zero are separate; no singular arbitrary-characteristic resolution transfer is made.
notes.text:
Use n1, n3 and n8. BFJ is applied ONLY at a smooth affine closed germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension≥2. Dimension one and zero are direct. Complete used published units were checked: setting; Sections 1.2–1.7; Definitions 2.1, 2.5 and Proposition 2.2; 2.7–2.8; 3.6–3.14; and the complete proofs of 3.9–3.10 through 3.18 and 3.22–3.25. Historical smooth resolution, usual multiplier subadditivity and smooth Izumi remain disclosed background.

BFJ's weak-nef Weil cone is the closed cone generated by formal-ideal divisors. Formal psh functions are finite and strongly continuous on quasi-monomials and have nef coefficient divisors. Their extension to ALL semivaluations is H_W(v)=inf_π H_W(r_πv). Proposition 2.7 gives H_W≤H_W∘r_π and decreasing refinement. The projective-limit statement 1.13 includes the all-support space.

Closed-simplex continuity in 3.11 is substantive. Multiplier profiles h_k=(1/k)log|L²(kW)| satisfy |h_k−H_W|≤A/k on divisorial points. Thinness A is bounded on a CLOSED simplex; the continuous multiplier profiles are uniformly Cauchy there and supply the extension on every face. Finite convexity alone would not give boundary continuity.

Correct 3.13: for nonzero formal psh g, B_j=L²(2^jg)+mhat^{4^j} and g_j=2^{-j}log|B_j|=max(2^{-j}log|L²(2^jg)|,−2^j). The exponents were visually checked on published page 475. Subadditivity makes the first term decrease; 3.9 gives quasi-monomial convergence; truncation also decreases. These ideals contain boundary powers, but early terms can be unit. Nonzero g has g(ord_m)<0 by 3.14, and the 3.9 estimate makes B_j proper for large j. Discard the finite prefix: approximants are EVENTUALLY proper primary. For g=0 use the UNIT ideal, not proper primary approximants decreasing to zero. The identically bottom function is outside finite formal psh on quasi-monomials and is adjoined separately through −N=−v(m^N).

Convergence is on ALL semivaluations. Given finite t>g(v), choose π with g(r_πv)<t by the all-retraction infimum, even if g(v)=bottom; then choose j with g_j(r_πv)<t. The inequalities g(v)≤g_j(v)≤g_j(r_πv)<t prove convergence. N1 contracts each completed primary exactly to R and the unit to the unit. Thus every BFJ function, with bottom adjoined, is in D_R. A finite continuous BFJ function is in C_R by the compact decreasing-continuous Dini open-cover argument.

Conversely finite real primary profiles are formal psh: their coefficients are nef, simplex evaluations continuous, and principalization/retractions give their canonical extension. For a uniform limit g, its finite divisorial coefficients define a weak-nef W. Actual 3.11 supplies H_W; uniform convergence on quasi-monomials and divisorial density on each simplex identify g with H_W there. The same uniform error bound passes through the infimum over ALL retractions, proving equality everywhere. Hence C_R is precisely the finite continuous BFJ subclass.

For a decreasing C_R-net g_i with infimum g, 3.14 gives g_i(v)≤g_i(ord_m) everywhere. If g(ord_m)=bottom, g is bottom everywhere. Otherwise its quasi-monomial lower bound C(v)g_i(ord_m)≤g_i(v) makes g finite there, and its finite coefficient limit W is weak-nef. On a simplex g is finite convex. For any x use its MINIMAL face, in whose relative interior finite convex functions are continuous. H_W is continuous on the whole face by 3.11; equality on its dense rational divisorial relative-interior points gives equality at x. Vertices are already divisorial. This avoids asserting closed-face continuity merely from convexity.

Finally extended infima commute over the Cartesian product of indices and ALL models:
g(v)=inf_i inf_π g_i(r_πv)=inf_π inf_i g_i(r_πv)=inf_π H_W(r_πv).
No nested-net flattening is used. D_R minus identically bottom is exactly the full BFJ formal psh class with its canonical all-semivaluation extension; D_R adjoins bottom. N8 transfers this to the geometric classes.

For a smooth DVR the boundary is a singleton. Powers of the parameter give all finite nonpositive constants in C and all extended nonpositive constants in D. The closed point is an actual effective Cartier divisor, with no contracted curve condition, giving the same geometric core. Dimension zero is the unique empty function. Arbitrary primary gauges follow n1's bounded positive homogeneous cocycle. Completion follows exact primary contraction, without a model-category equivalence claim.

notes.summary: Nonisolated cusp separates the ENTIRE finite-real raw cone from normalization-raw and C, with universal all-semivaluation error ≤2/k.
notes.detailedSummary: Explicit primary ideals approximate a compatible normalization profile including the conductor-infinite support. Two valuations give a strict inequality for every proper primary gauge, retained by every finite real combination but violated by the target. The finite-conductor locus is open, not generally closed.
notes.text:
Use n1, n3, n4 and n8. In characteristic zero let R=k[t²,t³,z]_(t²,t³,z), S=k[t,z]_(t,z), a=(t²,t³,z), and c=t²S. S is finite normal with the same fraction field. R has no t-degree-one terms; multiplication by t identifies the conductor exactly. R/c is localized k[z], and S/c its square-zero t-thickening. Their valuation boundaries coincide, so n1 makes normalization restriction a compact homeomorphism, including the nonminimal support (t). This is a two-dimensional nonisolated cusp.

Write s=w(t), u=w(z), b=z+t and B=w(b), with min(2s,u)=1. Allow infinite coordinates. A=w((b,t²))=min(B,2s) is bounded continuous and descends. For k≥1 set K_k=(b^k(z−kt),t²b^k,t^{2k+2})⊂R. The first generator's t-linear coefficient is kz^k−kz^k=0; the others have t-degree≥2. K_k is proper primary: its last generator puts t²,t³ in the radical and the first then puts z there.

Every generator has value≥kA. For the upper bound on EVERY semivaluation: if A=2s≤B, cancellation forces s=u=1, and the last generator has value kA+2. If A=B<2s and s≤u, normalization gives s≤1, and the second generator has value kA+2s≤kA+2. If s>u, including infinite s, then u=1 and B=w(z−kt)=1, so the first generator has value kA+1. Infinite u is in the second case. Thus 0≤v(K_k)/k−A≤2/k on ALL supports and cancellation cases. Therefore −A∈C_R and N_R. This is a universal proof, not a finite sample inference.

Separate the ENTIRE finite REAL raw cone. Let w_infty kill t and give z value one. Let w_star be monomial in (t,b), weights (1,2); z=b−t has value one. Both are normalized and A(w_infty)=1, A(w_star)=2. For ANY proper primary I, d=w_infty(I) is a positive integer. Choose f attaining d, with unit denominator, and expand in k[[t,z]]. There is no t-degree-one coefficient. Its degree-d homogeneous part has nonzero z^d coefficient and zero t z^{d−1} coefficient, so in characteristic zero it is not a scalar multiple of b^d. After substituting z=b−t it has a nonzero monomial t^{d−j}b^j with j<d, of w_star-value d+j≤2d−1. Other total degrees cannot cancel it; smaller-valued terms only strengthen the bound. Hence w_star(I)<2w_infty(I). Every nonzero finite real positive combination retains strictness; units contribute zero. A has equality, so A∉P_R and −A∉Q_R. N_R≠Q_R and C_R≠Q_R, while their uniform closures agree by n4.

The finite-conductor complement is OPEN and need not be closed: w_N(t)=N,w_N(z)=1 converge pointwise to w_infty, with conductor values 2N and infinity respectively. Thus conductor/N is not a uniform approximation error. N4 uses quotient estimates at infinity; n8 uses a fixed PRIMARY correction.

notes.text:

For the diagonal finite injection A=k[x,y]_(x,y)→A×A and J=((x,y²),(x²,y)), I_N=J^N∩A=(x,y²)^N∩(x²,y)^N. Both fibre ideals have m-order one. A monomial x^a y^b lies in I_N exactly when 2a+b≥2N and a+2b≥2N. Adding gives a+b≥ceil(4N/3); balanced exponents with that sum satisfy both inequalities. Thus order_m(I_N)=ceil(4N/3), with normalized limit 4/3 rather than one. The fibre profiles were incompatible. No general contraction-as-fibre-minimum shortcut is used. For I=(x+y,x³), v(I)=2 but r(v)(I)=1, contradicting printed r(v)(I)≥v(I). The negative function has the expected opposite inequality. The geometric boundary class is not identified with literal CLD/classical logarithmic radial extensions. For the node k[x,y]_(x,y)/(xy), normalization has two DVR centres. The tuple (−1,0) belongs to C_S and is compatible because conductor values are finite and no boundary pair is identified. N4 descends it to C_R and n8 puts it in C_geom. On a classical analytic node with two normalized discs, a zero logarithmic slope forces the nodal value≥0 by upper semicontinuity. A simultaneously negative slope tends to minus infinity at its origin; assigning a nodal value≥0 produces an interior maximum while outer-circle value is zero and other interior values negative, violating the subharmonic maximum principle. Thus this profile cannot be a literal classical psh radial extension.
